body.h2: How to make a Rotating Logo Reveal with Claude Code or Codex
body.body:
Cut a cube into three stacked slabs with a gap of 0.05 of the edge and spin it around a tilted axis (0.62, 0.74, 0.26). The spin runs 2.5s (0.2–2.7s) for 1.62 turns, about 1.5 of them in the first second, on expo.out cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) normalized to end exactly at 1, with no overshoot.

The end pose is isometric (rotX 35.264°, rotY −45°) with a vertex toward the camera, so the silhouette is a hexagon that matches the logo. A fixed orthographic camera grows it from 30% to 40% of frame height on the spin curve, and the three faces use three flat gray tones. At 5.0s a second shot flies three slabs in over 0.8s each, staggered 0.08s, and the lockup lands at 6.55–7.45s.

Press the copy button to send this recipe to Claude Code or Codex, or install the skill once with npx skills add krisyangdev/motionboard. The agent builds the slabs and the camera. Render an MP4 with HyperFrames, or port the GSAP timeline to your website.

en.alt: A grey cube split into three stacked layers, standing alone on a black background.
faq: A logo reveal is a short animation that builds up to a brand mark and holds it on screen. Common techniques include spinning, assembling pieces and drawing outlines. This recipe uses a rotation that decelerates onto the logo angle.
How long should a logo reveal be?
In this film the spin takes 2.5s and the stop is held for 2.3s, and the second shot lands the lockup in 0.9s. The last 0.8s of the rotation is a slow approach, which gives the stop a visible landing.
